Indicator: TB Pre-XDR treatment success rate
Cluster: The Social Protection, Community and Human Development cluster
ReasonforDeviation_Q1:
•	High death rate related to late presentation, delayed diagnosis and limited skills on drug resistant management associated with staff rotation and high staff turnover. 
•	High loss to follow up and treatment failure rate also contributed to low success rate.
CorrectiveAction_Q1:
•	Clinicians, data capturers and TB Coordinators were trained on EDRWEB dash board to identify early and follow up missing results necessary for adjusting treatment regimen. 
•	Community awareness campaigns on the importance of early presentation to clinic for TB treatment and adherence to treatment. 
•	Support Districts with technical working group meetings to ensure that all staff managing TB are updated on  DRTB management.
ReasonforDeviation_Q2: High death rate related to late presentation, delayed diagnosis and limited skills on drug resistant management associated with staff rotation and high staff turnover.
CorrectiveAction_Q2:
•	Clinicians, data capturers and TB Coordinators were trained on Electronic Drug Resistant Web-Based (EDRWEB) Tuberculosis Register  dash board to identify early and follow up missing results necessary for adjusting treatment regimen. 
•	Community awareness campaigns on the importance of early presentation to clinic for TB treatment and adherence to treatment. 
•	Support Districts with technical working group meetings to ensure that all staff managing TB are updated on Drug Resistant Tuberculosis (DRTB) management.
ReasonforDeviation_Q3: High death and lost-to-follow-up rates have contributed to the non-achievement of the success rate target, with Ethekwini reporting the highest rates.
CorrectiveAction_Q3:
•	Community awareness campaigns on the importance of early presentation to clinics for TB treatment and adherence to treatment. 
•	Implementation of:
o	drug-resistant clinical audit guidelines. 
o	DRTB literacy material. 
o	district technical advisory meetings to ensure that all clinicians are updated on Drug resistant TB management.
ReasonforDeviation_Q4:
•	High death and lost-to-follow-up rates have contributed to the non-achievement of the success rate target.
•	Treatment failure as patients present late with advanced disease and demise within a short period of being referred to the Centres of Excellence.
CorrectiveAction_Q4:
•	Community awareness campaigns on early clinic presentation for TB screening and treatment, with emphasize on the importance of adherence throughout treatment.
•	Convene regular District Technical Advisory Committee (DTAC) meetings to update clinicians on DR-TB management.
•	Implementation of the shorter DR-TB regimen which has shown an 86% success rate for Pre-XDR TB and 0% death.

ReasonforDeviation_Q2: Limited marketing of cervical cancer screening at the community and facility level.

•	Transition from using cytology as a primary method to Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) of human papillomaviruses (HPV) [HPV DNA] as primary screening method.
ReasonforDeviation_Q3:
•	Although KZN has implemented the transition from pap smear to human papillomaviruses (HPV) deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) testing, not all facilities have fully transitioned, leading to inconsistencies in screening methods and coverage.

•	Expand screening services to more locations, including rural and underserved areas, and consider mobile screening units or outreach programs to reach eligible women. 
•	Public awareness campaigns to educate women on the importance of cervical cancer screening and the benefits of HPV DNA testing. Provide educational materials and counselling to women at healthcare facilities.
